data.name: Serian
data.long_meaning: The name Serian may have roots in Hebrew, Greek, or Latin. In Hebrew, the name Ser is derived from the word 'sar', which means 'ruler' or 'chief'. In Greek, the name Serian may be derived from the word 'serios', which means 'serious' or 'earnest'. In Latin, the name Serian may be derived from the word 'servus', which means 'slave' or 'servant'. However, the exact origin of the name Serian is unknown. Regardless of its origin, the name Serian carries the meaning of a ruler or protector. In Christianity, the name Serian may be reminiscent of the Archangel Seraphiel, who is considered a protector and the commander of the seraphim, a class of angels in Christian and Jewish tradition.

historical_references.reference: Saint Serian, a fifth-century Syrian ascetic and bishop, is venerated as a saint in the Syriac and Coptic Orthodox Churches. He was a disciple of Saint Simeon Stylites the Elder and lived as a hermit in the Syrian desert. His relics were later transferred to Egypt where he is now venerated as a local saint.

He was a prominent opponent of General Belisarius and is described as having actively resisted Byzantine rule in the region.
